facts.statement: Huanghetitan is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Huanghetitan (meaning "Yellow River titan"), is a genus of sauropod dinosaur from the early Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: Huanghetitan was a basal titanosauriform that lived in what is now Gansu, China.
facts.quote: It was a basal titanosauriform which lived in what is now Gansu, China.

facts.statement: The type species Huanghetitan liujiaxiaensis was described by You et al. in 2006.
facts.quote: The type species, Huanghetitan liujiaxiaensis, was described by You et al. in 2006.

facts.statement: Huanghetitan liujiaxiaensis is known from fragmentary fossils found in the Lanzhou Basin, Gansu Province, in 2004.
facts.quote: It is known from fragmentary materials including two caudal vertebrae, an almost complete sacrum, rib fragments, and the left shoulder girdle, and was discovered in the eastern part of the Lanzhou Basin (Hekou Group) in the Gansu Province in 2004.

facts.statement: The second species, H. ruyangensis, was described in 2007 from fossils found in Ruyang County, Henan Province.
facts.quote: A second species, H. ruyangensis, was described in 2007 from the Aptian-Albian Haoling Formation of Ruyang County, China (Henan Province).

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analysis suggests H. ruyangensis is unlikely to be closely related to H. liujiaxiaensis and may require a new genus name.
facts.quote: A recent cladistic analysis has found that this species is unlikely to be closely related to H. liujiaxiaensis and requires a new genus name.

facts.statement: In 2019, Gregory S. Paul suggested that H. ruyangensis could have weighed between 45 and 55 metric tons based on comparisons with Patagotitan.
facts.quote: In 2019, Gregory S. Paul suggested that the dorsal rib of H. ruyangensis is about the same length as the titanosaur Patagotitan, and its sacrum may be similar in length, possibly suggesting a similar mass range of 45 – 55 MT.

facts.statement: A family named Huangetitanidae was proposed for Huanghetitan in 2007, but later analyses found it to be polyphyletic.
facts.quote: In 2007, Lü Junchang et al. created a new family for Huanghetitan, the Huangetitanidae, but this family found to be polyphyletic by Mannion et al.

facts.statement: Huanghetitan lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 125 and 89 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 125 a 89 millones de años, entre el Aptiense al Cenomaniense en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Huanghetitan is estimated from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)
